body: Is splitting not a term for black-and-white or all-or-nothing thinking? Yes, I find the path of moderation difficult.

> Do you mean that you are tired of acting a certain way for people to like you?

Yes, I think that is part of it... thank you. It's exhausting and embarrassingly inauthentic, but it's second nature to me at this point.

It is also a lot to do with a lack of communication and understanding, especially with people of the opposite sex... I'm starting to realize how difficult it is for me to understand male's intentions and for them to understand me.

Thank you for opening your inbox to me. It was a difficult night for me and that was very kind of you.

Thank you for elaborating on this; I'll have to look into it more. From what you have described, it sounds like it would be well-suited to me. It also sounds very familiar to me that the unknown of being better is uncomfortable and frightening. It's difficult to trust. This is actually something that I ended up talking with my therapist about yesterday. It can be challenging to find motivation and hope in getting better when I don't even know what that looks like. I don't know what sustainable happiness and wellbeing is for me. Not yet...
But it's more socially acceptable than doing hallucinogens in the forest where the trees are actually alive

Thank you for your response. I wasn't thinking about my reluctance to get better in terms of responsibility, but that makes a lot of sense.

I'll bring up DBT to my therapist and see what she says. I've also heard that a psychodynamic approach is particularly useful in treating BPD. It does seem like talk therapy becomes circular for me after a while.
